transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because this fear I have about rats has gotten really out of hand. I clean buildings for work, and it’s gotten to the point where just the thought that I might see one—like in a trash room, or a basement area, or one of those older parts of a building—can stop me from doing what I’m supposed to do.

I know, logically, it’s probably just an old building or a garbage area and not necessarily dangerous, but that doesn’t seem to matter in the moment. Even thinking about opening a door and maybe seeing a rat… I just can’t handle it sometimes. It’s affecting my job now, and that’s really why I came in.
Is your fear mainly about rats specifically?

Yes—rats specifically. I mean, it’s the thought of seeing a rat that really sets me off. Like if I’m at work and I have to go into a trash room, or one of those older basement areas, my mind just goes right to, “What if there’s a rat in there?” And even though part of me knows it’s probably just an old building or garbage area and not actually dangerous, I still can’t make myself do parts of the cleaning sometimes. It’s gotten bad enough that it’s interfering with my job.
Do you do anything over and over, like checking, cleaning, or other rituals, to try to reduce the fear about rats?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like a ritual, I mean. I’m not, like, counting things or washing my hands a certain number of times or checking a door over and over in some exact way, if that’s what you mean.

I do kind of… hesitate a lot, and I’ll stand outside a room longer than I probably should, trying to listen or trying to convince myself it’s okay to go in. But I don’t know if that counts as “doing something over and over.” It’s more like I get stuck because I’m scared. I might look around or pause before opening a trash room door, but it’s not some routine that makes the fear go away. Honestly, it usually doesn’t make it go away much at all.
Outside of situations where there might be rats, do you still feel anxious a lot of the time?

Um… I don’t know that I’d say I’m anxious all the time, no. I mean, life is stressful, sure, and work can be stressful, especially when I’m thinking about what areas I might have to clean that day. But when it’s not connected to that—like if I’m at home, or doing regular errands, or I’m somewhere where rats aren’t even on my mind—I don’t think I’m walking around nervous for no reason.

It’s more like my anxiety kind of switches on when there’s a chance, or even just the idea, that there could be a rat. Then I can get really worked up. But outside of that… I guess I feel more normal? Or at least not constantly anxious.
When you actually see a rat, do you get a sudden surge of intense fear or panic?

Yes. It’s like it happens before I even have time to think. If I actually see one—or even if I hear scratching near a wall, or something moves by a pipe and I think it might be a rat—my whole body just reacts right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake, and I get this really strong feeling like I have to get out of there immediately.

It’s not like I calmly decide, “Oh, I’m scared.” It’s more like my body decides for me. I freeze for a second and then I just want to back away or leave the area before I can even think straight.
